data.name: Abyaz
data.gender_notes: Abyaz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, the name Abyaz is derived from the word 'ab' meaning 'father' and 'yaz' meaning 'horses'. In Islamic history, Abyaz was the name of the father of Salman Al-Farsi, a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The name Abyaz carries the meaning “Father of horses” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Abyaz usually hope their child will grow to embody father of horses and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of strength and loyalty, just as a father is to his children and a horse is to its rider.
data.etymology: Abyaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Father of horses.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abyaz total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Abyaz" carries a rich cultural heritage as it is associated with Salman Al-Farsi, a highly revered figure in Islamic history. Salman was a Persian slave who was taken to Mecca as a young man and later embraced Islam. He was a valiant companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and played a significant role in spreading the message of Islam. Abyaz, his father's name, holds importance in the imposing legacy of Salman's life and his contributions to Islamic history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Abyaz" also holds spiritual significance, as the etymology of the name can be traced back to the Prophet's companion and his familial lineage. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that one's name can have an impact on one's character and destiny. The name Abyaz, meaning 'father of horses,' might symbolize the idea of 'love and protection.' This idea reflects the role of parents in nurturing and guiding their children to reach their full potential. Additionally, horses often symbolize power, strength, and endurance in Islamic culture, which could further contribute to the spiritual significance of the name.
